newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson tops ADR market.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson tops ADR market.

text.p: Swedish telephone equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson was the most-active issue Thursday in a quiet May Day market for American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Ericsson rose 1/4 to 33-7/8 on moderate volume of 1.2 million shares by midday, putting it at the top of the ADRs' volume list.

The shares have risen from a closing price of about 29-1/2 on Friday, when they fell after the company released strong first quarter earnings clouded by a negative cash flow and weaker sales in mobile systems.
"Merrill Lynch yesterday had positive comments about the stock, not to mention that the U.S. market is incredibly strong," a trader said of Ericsson.
"Also, Sweden's market is closed (for the May Day holiday) and that gives guys a good opportunity to trade."
Merrill Lynch raised Ericsson to near-term buy from accumulate and named it its focus stock of the week.
Traders said the ADR market was quiet since many European and Latin American exchanges were closed for the holiday.

Among other European shares, Royal Dutch Petroleum Co fell two to 178-1/4 after Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported flat first quarter results and issued a cautious outlook for oil prices and refining margins.
Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc fell 1-1/8 to 105-1/4. Royal Dutch/Shell is 60 percent owned by Royal Dutch and 40 percent by Shell.
London-based news and information company Reuters Holdings Plc rose 2-3/4 to 64-3/8 after company presentations to analysts and fund managers in New York.
Dutch electronics company Philips Electronics NV also rose 1-3/8 to 54-7/8.
Advancers led decliners 240 to 187 among 806 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.21 percent and volume at midday was 30 million shares.
